record.paper_title: Semantic Subtyping: Challenges, Perspectives, and Open Problems
record.original_question: For semantic-subtyping systems with negation types, especially systems like Duce and local variants of π where typing values may require infinitely many negated types or schematic representations, is the need for 'enough points' and explicit deduction of negated types an unavoidable feature of semantic subtyping, or can one recover simple minimum typing and a set-theoretic semantics without such infinitary or schematic machinery?

evidence.quote: So once more the question is whether this problem is a limitation of semantic subtyping or it is implicit in the usage of negation types. And as it can be 'solved' in the case case of π by considering the full system instead of just the local version, is it possible to find similar (and meaningful) solutions in other cases (notably for Duce)?

Finally, it would be interesting to check whether the semantic subtyping type system could be used to define a denotational semantics of the language by relating the semantic of an expression with the set of its types and (since our type system is closed by finite intersections and subsumption) build a filter model [BCD83].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a typed lambda-calculus-style language equipped with a semantic subtyping discipline, in which types are interpreted set-theoretically and the type connectives include intersection, union, and negation. In such a system, the subtyping relation s ≤ t is defined extensionally, by interpreting types as sets of values and requiring [[s]] ⊆ [[t]]. Two representative systems of this kind are: (i) "Duce", a calculus of higher-order functions with full Boolean type connectives whose semantics requires an "enough points" property to ensure that function types are nontrivially distinguished, and (ii) "local" variants of a calculus π in which typing rules use only finitely many derivation steps but for which assigning the most precise type to a value can require taking an infinite intersection of negated atomic types, or equivalently a schematic (universally quantified over a family of negations) representation.

Concretely, in such systems the following two phenomena arise:

(a) "Enough points": to validate the set-theoretic interpretation of negated function types, one must postulate that the model contains sufficiently many values (points) so that distinct function types are inhabited by distinct values; without this, the lattice of types collapses in undesired ways.

(b) "Explicit deduction of negated types": for a value v to receive its minimum (principal) type, the typing derivation must explicitly mention an unbounded or infinite family of negated types ¬t_i, so that minimum typing is no longer a finitary syntactic procedure but requires schematic or infinitary rules.

The problem is the following. Determine whether these two features — the "enough points" assumption on the underlying model and the explicit (possibly infinitary or schematic) deduction of negated types — are intrinsically necessary for any type system that

  (1) admits negation types,
  (2) is sound and complete with respect to a set-theoretic interpretation of types (so that s ≤ t iff [[s]] ⊆ [[t]]),
  (3) supports a notion of minimum (principal) type for every typable value, derivable by finitary rules,

or whether one can design a semantic-subtyping type system meeting (1)–(3) in which neither an "enough points" hypothesis nor infinitary/schematic negation introduction is required. In particular, exhibit either:

  (A) a proof (e.g. an impossibility theorem) that any type system satisfying (1)–(3) must include some form of "enough points" assumption and some infinitary or schematic mechanism for deriving negated types; or

  (B) a concrete type system, with a finitary minimum-typing algorithm and a set-theoretic semantics validating sound and complete subtyping with negation, that avoids both features, and in particular yields a system for higher-order functions (analogous to Duce) free of these requirements.

As a related sub-question, determine whether such a semantic-subtyping type system, being closed under finite intersections and subsumption, can be used to define a denotational semantics of the underlying language by associating to each expression the set of its types and constructing a filter model in the style of intersection type theories.
artifact.status_search_result: No specific published resolution of this question could be verified. The question concerns foundational design choices in semantic subtyping with negation types and appears to remain an open research direction; a definitive solved/open determination from authoritative sources is not available.
